hypotheses.statement: Release 2.14.1 changed ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS from 825 to 8.25, and the order handler fails parsing it (the config also holds AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP)

claims.text: Release 2.14.1 changed one setting, ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS, from 825 to 8.25 (config revision cfg-42); no code changed.
Only instances on 2.14.1 fail: from 14:02 version 2.14.1 errors on most requests while 2.14.0 stays at its baseline rate.
Every new error is ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '8.25' in compute_totals (orders/pricing.py line 37), first seen at 14:02:04 on 2.14.1 only.
The failing trace reads ORDER_TAX_RATE_BPS at the failing frame, compute_totals, on config revision cfg-42.
The overall HTTP 500 rate rose with each rollout step: 5% at 14:02, 25% at 14:07, 50% at 14:12.

hypotheses.confirm_test: Error rate by version: only 2.14.1 fails; restoring 825 on a 2.14.1 instance clears the ValueError.
hypotheses.refute_test: 2.14.0 instances failing with the same ValueError, or errors starting before 14:02.

hypotheses.statement: orders-db connection failures cause the HTTP 500 responses

claims.text: Dependency health records one connection reset on orders-db at 14:04:11, on orders-api-b, recovered on retry.

hypotheses.confirm_test: Database errors on failing requests, on both versions.
hypotheses.refute_test: orders-db healthy and the old version unaffected.

hypotheses.statement: Payment gateway timeouts cause the HTTP 500 responses

claims.text: TimeoutError from the payment gateway appears in the logs on POST /v1/orders.

hypotheses.confirm_test: Timeouts rising with the failures, on both versions.
hypotheses.refute_test: Timeouts at their usual rate, on 2.14.0 only.
